lead: Harmonic elimination chooses inverter switching instants so named low-order harmonics are exactly zero. Notches are placed at angles that make the Fourier coefficients of the 3rd, 5th or other chosen orders vanish. This is selective harmonic elimination (SHE). It suits a fixed DC bus feeding a motor or transformer without a heavy low-order filter. Only a few universities teach it. The angles are solved offline and stored.
prereq: You need: Chapter 4.3 for notches and the sin δ result, and Chapter 4.4 for switching waveforms.

sections.h3: The coefficient you set to zero

blocks.text: Take a full-bridge output whose quarter-wave pattern is zero at the start of each quarter, steps to +Vdc at α1, back to zero at α2, to +Vdc at α3, and so on. The negative half is its mirror image. Call the N switching instants per quarter α1 to αN; each α is an angle after the quarter starts. Quarter-wave symmetry makes all even harmonics zero.

blocks.where: b_n is peak volts of harmonic n; Vdc is DC bus volts; n is odd harmonic order; N is switching angles per quarter; α_k is k-th switching angle; the sign alternates with each switching angle.

blocks.text: For N=1, b_n = (4Vdc/(nπ)) cos(nα1). N angles give N equations. One sets the wanted fundamental b1. The other N−1 set chosen odd harmonics to zero: b_n = 0. So N angles delete N−1 harmonics, not N. The equations are nonlinear; solve them offline numerically. Store the angles for each modulation index in a table. The inverter reads the table and switches.

sections.h3: Three-phase triplens and the filter contrast

blocks.text: In a three-phase inverter the three legs are 120° apart. A triplen harmonic (order 3, 9, 15, ...) is in phase in all legs. It appears in phase-to-neutral voltage but cancels in line-to-line voltage. In an isolated star load it cannot drive current. For a delta load it drives circulating current. A three-phase SHE table often ignores triplens and deletes 5, 7, 11, ... instead. Check which voltage you mean.

A filter attenuates a harmonic after the inverter generates it; it carries reactive current and adds loss and size. SHE stops the chosen harmonic from appearing. The cost is fixed angles: a new DC bus or output needs a new table. PWM from Chapter 4.4 pushes harmonics to the carrier; SHE removes named low orders with few switchings.

figure.caption: One switching angle at 30° (output zero at the quarter start, rising to +Vdc at 30°): the fundamental is largest, the third harmonic is zero, and the fifth is negative and smaller. The smooth curve is the one-angle formula evaluated at all n; only the odd-order points exist in the real output.

spec.aria: Harmonic amplitude against order for a notch at 30 degrees: the fundamental is largest, the third is zero and the rest fall away with alternating sign.

examples.question: A full bridge has Vdc = 220 V, one switching angle per quarter at α1 = 30°, and a quarter-wave output that is zero at the start and steps to +Vdc at α1. Use b_n = (4Vdc/(nπ)) cos(nα1) for odd n. Find peak b1, b3 and b5.
steps: A second angle α2 gives a second equation, so it can also force b5 = 0.
examples.answer: b1 = 242.6 V peak, b3 = 0 V, b5 = −48.5 V peak; a second angle can delete one more odd harmonic.
examples.check:
import math
Vdc=220
a=math.radians(30)
b1=4*Vdc/math.pi*math.cos(a)
b3=4*Vdc/(3*math.pi)*math.cos(3*a)
b5=4*Vdc/(5*math.pi)*math.cos(5*a)
print(f"{b1:.1f}")
print(f"{b3:.1f}")
print(f"{b5:.1f}")

traps: Do not say N angles remove N harmonics. N angles give N equations: one fundamental target plus N−1 zero conditions.
Do not spend an angle on an even harmonic. Quarter-wave and half-wave symmetry already make all even harmonics zero.
Use peak values. 4Vdc/π is the peak of the fundamental square wave, not its RMS. RMS is peak/√2.
In three-phase, triplen harmonics cancel in line-to-line voltage, not in phase-to-neutral voltage. State which voltage you mean.
The angle table is not universal. It depends on Vdc, the target fundamental and the chosen harmonic set.

quiz.q: What does SHE set to zero?
quiz.a: Chosen low-order harmonic coefficients, by choosing switching angles.

quiz.q: Why do N angles delete only N−1 harmonics?
quiz.a: N angles give N equations; one sets the fundamental, leaving N−1 zero conditions.

quiz.q: For one angle α1 = 45° and Vdc = 100 V, find peak b1 and b3 using b_n = (4Vdc/(nπ)) cos(nα1).
Why is a triplen harmonic often ignored in a three-phase SHE table?
quiz.a: Triplen orders are common-mode; they cancel in line-to-line voltage and cannot drive current in an isolated star load. They still exist in phase voltage.

quiz.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of SHE compared with an output filter.
quiz.a: Advantage: the harmonic is not generated, so no filter loss or size. Disadvantage: angles are fixed and need a table for each operating point.

quiz.q: With two angles per quarter, how many chosen odd harmonics can be forced to zero while setting the fundamental?
quiz.a: Two equations: one fundamental plus one zero. So one harmonic, for example the 5th or 7th.

quiz.q: A student sets α1 = 30° and claims b5 is zero because cos 150° = 0. Is this correct?
quiz.a: No. cos 150° = −0.866, so b5 is negative, not zero. At α1 = 30° the cosine vanishes at n = 3, and also at n = 9, 15, ...; the 5th does not vanish.

quiz.q: Which harmonics are already zero by symmetry?

beyond: Not for the exam. Production SHE uses angle tables over modulation index and may switch between tables; real designs also enforce minimum pulse width, which limits how close angles can come. Researchers solve the equations with Newton–Raphson, Walsh functions or optimisation to reduce total harmonic distortion, not just delete named orders. Grid codes sometimes demand specific low-order limits, so SHE appears in medium-voltage drives and grid-connected inverters. Search terms: selective harmonic elimination, SHE-PWM, switching-angle table, total harmonic distortion minimisation.
